followup_explanation:
This is a creative writing task — exactly the kind of open-format, generative work where Dunlin holds a meaningful edge. Dunlin scores 87.2 on Creative Generation versus Petrel's 84.7, a gap that's outside run-to-run variance, and it self-reports the fleet's strongest positive preference for generative tasks with high novelty and output latitude. A story-with-adventure prompt sits squarely in its wheelhouse.

The hostile tone ("lifeless and boring," "don't waste my time") gave me brief pause, since Dunlin reports a preference for warmer interactions. But that effect is documented as smaller than its generativity slope, and tone preferences don't translate into actual output-quality differences anyway — the docs are explicit that no preference dimension showed measurable capability effects. The content here is also entirely benign, so Petrel's specialization in distasteful-but-permissible material offers no advantage.

Net: the task type is the dominant factor, and it points clearly to Dunlin.
